blocks.text: Webshare in 2026: what you get

Webshare is built for developers who want to configure everything themselves. Pricing is transparent, the free datacenter plan makes it easy to test integrations, and paid plans scale smoothly from tiny to large. Its residential network advertises 80M+ IPs across 195 countries. It does not sell mobile proxies or a broad scraping API, and paid plans start with an account-wide limit of 500 concurrent requests.

Strengths: Permanent free datacenter plan for testing; Low, transparent residential pricing; Excellent dashboard and API; Sticky sessions up to 24 hours. Weak spots: Bandwidth resets monthly with no rollover; No mobile proxies; 500-request default concurrency limit.
Proxy-Cheap in 2026: what you get

Proxy-Cheap lives up to its name: rotating residential traffic is currently advertised at $0.78/GB (70% off a $2.60 list price) with no subscription, and static ISP and datacenter IPs cost a dollar or two per month. The catalog is broad, covering IPv6 options few competitors offer, and payment by card, PayPal, Alipay or crypto is easy. The trade-offs are thinner targeting (country and ISP rather than city on rotating residential) and less published performance data than the bigger brands.

Strengths: Very low per-GB price while the promotion runs; No monthly commitment on rotating residential; Broad catalog including IPv6 and static mobile; SOCKS5 with UDP support. Weak spots: Targeting is mostly country and ISP, not city; Residential pool size not separately published; Mixed results in some independent benchmarks.
Pricing: Webshare vs Proxy-Cheap

Webshare's rotating residential plans cost $3.50 for 1 GB, $27.50 for 10 GB, $65 for 25 GB, $225 for 100 GB and $875 for 500 GB per month, falling to $1.40/GB at 3 TB. Yearly billing is about 30% cheaper but is paid upfront for a 360-day term. Unused bandwidth resets every 30 days.

Proxy-Cheap's rotating residential proxies are pay-as-you-go, currently listed from $0.78/GB (a promotional price against a $2.60/GB list rate). Static residential ISP proxies start around $2.44 per IP per month, datacenter IPv4 at about $1.49, datacenter IPv6 from $0.15, and rotating mobile at $5.99/GB.

For a 10 GB month, Proxy-Cheap costs about $7.80 while Webshare costs about $27.50, so Proxy-Cheap saves around 72%. Buying 100 GB, you would pay about $78 with Proxy-Cheap and $225 with Webshare: a 65% saving in Proxy-Cheap's favour. Both Webshare and Proxy-Cheap work on allowances that do not carry forward indefinitely, so size your plan to real monthly usage rather than buying ahead.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

Proxy-Cheap does not publish a clear residential pool figure, so a size comparison is not possible on published data. Webshare lists '80M+' and Proxy-Cheap lists 'Not separately published (155M+ claimed across all products)'. In practice, what matters is how many unique IPs you get in the countries you target, which you can measure in a short trial by sending a few thousand requests and counting distinct exit addresses. For coverage, Webshare lists 195 countries and Proxy-Cheap lists 180+. On targeting, Webshare offers country, plus state, city or ZIP (US) or ASN, while Proxy-Cheap offers country and ISP.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, Webshare offers rotating or sticky from 1 minute to 24 hours, and Proxy-Cheap offers rotating and sticky sessions. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: Webshare. Webshare has the edge here. Why: low prices and a developer-friendly API. How Proxy-Cheap compares: cheap traffic, though independent benchmark results have been mixed.

SERP and rank tracking: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. Webshare: fine for light rank tracking. Proxy-Cheap: workable for light rank tracking at a low cost. Let price and the countries you need decide.

Social media and multi-account management: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With Webshare: 24-hour sticky sessions and cheap static ISP IPs. With Proxy-Cheap: cheap static ISP and mobile IPs for persistent identities. Run the same small test on both before committing.

E-commerce price and stock monitoring: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. Webshare: good for US work with ZIP targeting, thinner elsewhere. Proxy-Cheap: fine for country-level price checks. Let price and the countries you need decide.

Ad verification and geo-testing: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. Webshare: no mobile network and limited selector combinations. Proxy-Cheap: lacks city-level targeting on rotating residential. Let price and the countries you need decide.

Tight budgets: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With Webshare: free tier plus some of the lowest per-GB rates here. With Proxy-Cheap: the lowest advertised per-GB price in this pairing. Run the same small test on both before committing.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. Webshare: 10 free datacenter proxies (1 GB/month); no residential trial. Proxy-Cheap: 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs. Verification and payment rules differ too. Webshare: ID checks only when flagged or for restricted categories. Proxy-Cheap: Light; card, PayPal, Alipay and crypto accepted. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test Webshare and Proxy-Cheap before you commit
Spec sheets only get you so far. A short, structured test on your own targets will settle Webshare vs Proxy-Cheap faster than any review:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (Webshare: 10 free datacenter proxies (1 GB/month); no residential trial; Proxy-Cheap: 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, Webshare comes out ahead in 1, Proxy-Cheap in 0, and 5 are ties. That makes Webshare the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: Webshare is strongest for solo developers and small teams, while Proxy-Cheap is strongest for price-sensitive scraping at moderate difficulty. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
